text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has fallen nearly 18% over two weeks, with today's modest 1.2% decline continuing a sharp downtrend that accelerated after the midterm elections on November 4th. The sharpest drops came on November 4th and 5th, coinciding with oil prices falling as investors reassessed geopolitical risk following the elections — US oil fell to $99.64 a barrel today from higher levels earlier in the week. Refinery utilization remains solid at 94.5%, so the move reflects broader crude price weakness rather than operational problems at the company itself.

The election result appears to have triggered a rotation away from traditional energy stocks, with concern that a Democratic Congress could favor renewables like offshore wind and solar over fossil fuels. While some analysts warn that renewed U.S.-Iran tensions could push oil back above $100, markets are currently pricing in lower near-term oil demand and the political headwinds facing refiners regardless of crude price direction.
